title: Releasing comfort for a different home

captions.physics: Carrying out a needed domestic change
captions.energy: Holding to a restrictive familiar form

meaning: Your domestic movement offers support when attachment to ready comfort allows an old form to end after it has begun obstructing both people’s present life.
text: You can change domestic routines through directed action: noticing a need, choosing a suitable answer and handling practical difficulty. The Chariot in the physical position of Muladhara describes moving towards a result. The Devil in energy tests your footing through attachment to familiar comfort that is hard to leave. Death in emotions experiences a former form of life ending. Movement may therefore stall despite a clear need: new arrangements require effort and acknowledgement that a known convenience will no longer offer peace in precisely its previous way.

For example, a large sofa obstructs other shared activities in the room. You seek a replacement, but every option is compared with familiar evening rest and feels like loss. **A suitable new arrangement need not preserve everything old simultaneously.** You can cherish the former way while recognising its limit. Domestic action becomes transition towards current needs, leaving room for an ending without either keeping everything untouched or immediately ceasing to miss the familiar.

The difficulty is preserving all existing comfort while freeing space at the same time. Options multiply, effort grows and the room stays unchanged. Releasing some convenience seems riskier than endless searching. Support becomes clearer when change recognises choice’s actual cost and the new has room without completely compensating every lost detail of the former routine. Its different usefulness can then become visible.
